t.Setenv("TS_VERIFY_LIVE", "")
	for _, test := range []struct {
		args      []string
		want      string
		wantError bool
	}{
		{args: []string{"--help"}, want: "Usage: ts-orch"},
		{args: []string{"verify", "--help"}, want: "opt in"},
		{args: []string{"verify"}, want: "requires --live", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"log-scan", "--help"}, want: "--fly-app"},
		{args: []string{"dashboard", "--help"}, want: "three observed controllers"},
		{args: []string{"dashboard", "check"}, want: "requires --gru-token-file", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"cost"}, want: "Usage: ts-orch cost report"},
		{args: []string{"cost", "report"}, want: "needs --region", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"network", "--help"}, want: "--all"},
		{args: []string{"network", "check", "unexpected"}, want: "no positional arguments", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"bootstrap", "--help"}, want: "sign-anchor"},
		{args: []string{"release", "--help"}, want: "sign-binary"},
		{args: []string{"image", "--help"}, want: "build-offline"},
		{args: []string{"netbird", "--help"}, want: "install"},
		{args: []string{"netbird", "path-audit", "--help"}, want: "--expected-ip"},
		{args: []string{"netbird", "path-audit"}, want: "requires --vault-id", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"netbird", "sync", "--help"}, want: "prune-peers"},
		{args: []string{"netbird", "inventory", "unexpected"}, want: "no positional arguments", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"oci-region", "--help"}, want: "preview"},
		{args: []string{"oci-region", "import-image", "--help"}, want: `unknown oci-region command "import-image"`, wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"oci-region", "import-image", "--qcow2", "candidate.qcow2", "--sha256", strings.Repeat("a", 64)}, want: `unknown oci-region command "import-image"`, wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"qualification", "--help"}, want: "firecracker"},
		{args: []string{"qualification", "firecracker", "--help"}, want: "prepare-base"},
		{args: []string{"runtime-priority", "--help"}, want: "probe-admission"},
		{args: []string{"ouroboros", "--help"}, want: "fly-secrets"},
		{args: []string{"vault", "--help"}, want: "render"},
		{args: []string{"disaster-recovery", "--help"}, want: "does not rebuild"},
		{args: []string{"disaster-recovery", "replicate"}, want: "requires --config", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"disaster-recovery", "drill"}, want: "unknown disaster-recovery command", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"vault", "put"}, want: "put requires", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"ouroboros", "fly-secrets"}, want: "fly-secrets requires", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"bootstrap", "verify-anchor"}, want: "verify-anchor requires", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"release", "publish"}, want: "publish requires", wantError: true},
		{args: []string{"misspelled"}, want: "unknown command", wantError: true},
	} {
		t.Run(strings.Join(test.args, " "), func(t *testing.T) {
			var output bytes.Buffer
			err := Run(t.Context(), test.args, &output)
			if test.wantError {
				if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), test.want) {
					t.Fatalf("error = %v, want %q", err, test.want)
				}
				if output.Len() != 0 {
					t.Fatalf("failed command wrote data: %q", output.String())
				}
			} else if err != nil || !strings.Contains(output.String(), test.want) {
				t.Fatalf("output = %q, error = %v", output.String(), err)
			}
		})
	}

const usage = `Usage: ts-orch log-scan --vault-id OCID [--netbird COMMAND] [--since 20m] [--top 10] [--node NAME]... [--fly-app NAME]...

Counts WARN and ERROR records per service and node over the last --since.
Without --node it reads every server the NetBird client lists: each peer
named like a cell node or server (ts-gru-1, gru-1-ctl-1). Each node is read
from its journal (units terrascale-orchestrator*: the
controller, the host agent, embedded NATS and the TerraBase and ts-auth
members) over "ts-orch netbird ssh" as the automation user, with the same
--vault-id and --netbird. Each --fly-app is read from "fly logs --no-tail",
which holds only its last 100 lines. Then lists the --top most frequent
classes. Exits unsuccessfully when a node or app cannot be read.
`

  sign-external-seed-reservation
  publish-external-seed-reservation
  observe-external-seed
  sign-external-seed-completion
  publish-external-seed-completion
  sign-slot-retirement
`

type command struct {
	ctx    context.Context
	output io.Writer
}

// Run executes a bootstrap command without starting the controller or host agent.
func Run(ctx context.Context, args []string, output io.Writer) error {
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	writer := commandio.NewWriter(output)
	var err error
	if len(args) == 1 && (args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" || args[0] == "help") {
		_, err = io.WriteString(writer, usage)
	} else {
		err = (command{ctx: ctx, output: writer}).run(args)
	}
	return errors.Join(err, ctx.Err(), writer.Err())
}

const usage = `Usage: ts-orch vault <command> [flags]

  put     --vault-id OCID --key-id OCID --compartment-id OCID --name NAME --file FILE
      Store FILE once as secret NAME (operator ~/.oci/config). An existing secret is
      never replaced: put reads it back and fails unless it equals FILE.
  render  --vault-id OCID --scope SCOPE --template FILE --out FILE
      On a host, as root: replace each {{KEY}} of the template with the JSON-quoted
      secret <scope>-<key>, read with the instance principal, and write FILE
      atomically, mode 0600, in a private tmpfs directory with swap disabled.
  deliver --cell REGION --service SERVICE --refs FILE --dir /run/DIRECTORY [--refresh 1m] [--once]
      Read a JSON map of keys to {vault, name} using the instance principal.
      Publish owner-only files named by lowercasing each key. Poll CURRENT versions;
      changed versions atomically replace files without redeploying the consumer.
  version --vault-id OCID --name NAME --secret-id OCID --expect-current N --file FILE [--instance-principal]
      Publish an owner-supplied value as a new CURRENT version with If-Match.
      On any uncertain result, reread CURRENT before retrying. Never generates keys.

Output names secrets and OCIDs, never a value. See docs/secrets.md.
`

// maxValue bounds one secret; OCI refuses bundles over 25 KB.
const maxValue = 16 << 10

var placeholderRE = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\}\}`)

// Run dispatches the vault commands.
func Run(ctx context.Context, args []string, output io.Writer) error {
	if len(args) == 0 || args[0] == "help" || args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" {
		_, err := io.WriteString(output, usage)
		return err
	}
	flags := flag.NewFlagSet("vault "+args[0], flag.ContinueOnError)
	flags.SetOutput(io.Discard)
	vaultID := flags.String("vault-id", "", "the Vault OCID")
	keyID := flags.String("key-id", "", "the Vault master key OCID")
	compartmentID := flags.String("compartment-id", "", "the compartment of a new secret")
	name := flags.String("name", "", "the secret name")
	file := flags.String("file", "", "the secret value")
	secretID := flags.String("secret-id", "", "the exact secret OCID")
	expected := flags.Int64("expect-current", 0, "the current version the owner read")
	instancePrincipal := flags.Bool("instance-principal", false, "publish as the regional service principal")
	scope := flags.String("scope", "", "the secret name prefix, a cell such as gru-1")
	template := flags.String("template", "", "the template to render")
	out := flags.String("out", "", "the rendered file")
	cell := flags.String("cell", "", "the region name, gru or sfo")
	service := flags.String("service", "", "the owner service")
	refs := flags.String("refs", "", "the public Vault reference JSON file")
	directory := flags.String("dir", "", "the private tmpfs delivery directory")
	refresh := flags.Duration("refresh", time.Minute, "the CURRENT version polling interval")
	once := flags.Bool("once", false, "deliver the current versions once")
	fileNames := flags.Bool("file-names", false, "reference keys are exact filenames for existing signed paths")
	if err := flags.Parse(args[1:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if flags.NArg() != 0 {
		return errors.New("unexpected vault arguments")
	}
	if err := safeEnv(); err != nil {
		return err
	}

func ouroborosUsage() string {
	var projects []string
	for _, project := range Projects {
		projects = append(projects, project.Name+" (database "+project.Database+")")
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf(`Usage: ts-orch ouroboros <command> [flags]

  bootstrap    --plan FILE --client-url URL --admin-url URL --member NODE
               --member-ca FILE --dashboard-credential-file FILE
               [--management-listener client|admin]
               [--owner-email EMAIL --ts-auth-instance SLUG --ts-auth-key-file FILE
                [--ts-auth-url URL]]
      Find or create, in the production TerraBase, TerraScale's organization
      %[1]s and its projects
        %[2]s
      through one member's Management and admin APIs, acting as %[3]s,
      which so owns a new organization. For each project, store its ID and,
      unless the Vault holds one, a newly issued documents:read/write API key
      narrowed to its database in the cell's Vault; read both back and check
      the key reaches the database. Prints one line of tenant IDs per project.
      Management requests use the client listener, or with
      --management-listener admin the loopback admin listener, the only one
      that accepts the credential from TerraBase TS-519 on.
      With --owner-email and --management-listener admin, once that address
      has signed in to ts-auth: add its ts-auth user as a member, make it the
      owner and keep %[3]s as an admin. Prints the steps taken.
  fly-secrets  --plan FILE
      Hand the dashboard, Fly app %[4]s, TERRABASE_URL, TERRABASE_PROJECT_ID,
      TERRABASE_DATABASE and TERRABASE_API_KEY, and its ts-auth client

func Runbook(target RecoveryTarget) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf(`Break-glass quorum-loss recovery for cell %[1]s (survivor %[2]s)

Use only when a majority of controllers is permanently lost and normal slot
replacement cannot run (authority needs JetStream quorum). The most recent
writes acknowledged only by lost controllers may be lost.

 1. Operator: confirm the lost controllers' instances are TERMINATED in OCI
    and cannot return. Terminate any that still exist.
 2. Operator: stop the controller service on every survivor.
 3. On every survivor:  ts-orch cluster recover-quorum preflight --config <controller.json>
 4. On every survivor:  ts-orch cluster recover-quorum backup --config <controller.json> --out <dir>
    then:               ts-orch cluster recover-quorum verify-backup --dir <dir>
    Copy each backup off the host before continuing.
 5. For each lost peer slot, render its retirement request on a survivor:
    ts-orch cluster recover-quorum render-retirement --config <controller.json> \
        --slot <slot> --out <dir>
    (or copy a <slot>.retirement-request.json the leader rendered before
    quorum was lost), then root-sign it offline with
    ts-orch bootstrap sign-slot-retirement.
 6. Operator: start the controller service on every survivor again. A lone
    survivor waits for quorum without authority, but its broker runs. The
    data-bearing survivor must be running before any lost peer boots:
    re-founded peers start with empty stores, and two of them without the
    survivor could elect an empty metadata group of their own.
 7. On the seed survivor, as the controller service account, one lost slot
    at a time:
    ts-orch cluster recover-quorum refound --config <controller.json> --slot <slot> \
        --retirement <slot>.retirement --backup <dir>
    refound refuses while the survivor broker is not running, while another
    slot has an incomplete re-founded attempt, or while the slot re-founded
    before has not reported current; after relaunching it waits until the
    re-founded slot reports current. Each lost slot
    is relaunched as its next ledger attempt with the same private IP and
    NATS server name, so it rejoins the survivor's raft groups with an empty
    store (the survivor's longer log wins every election) instead of needing
    a single-node restart. Wait until the re-founded peer reports current in
    the metadata group before re-founding the next slot.
 8. Confirm with the operator status commands that every stream reports
    three current replicas. Streams keep their R3 configuration.

A literal single-node restart is not offered: the signed topology fixes the
slot count, and a standalone server does not load R3 streams from its store.
If the seed slot itself is lost, stop here: seed handoff needs a new signed
founder authority.
`, target.Cell, target.Slot)
}
